ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 4-6-0 so far, losers of five straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they play fast, wide-open games and hit everything that moves.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 8-2-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in seven of their eleven games.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but they spend a lot of time in the box.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 4-4-2 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They find a way to get their shots past the blockers and rarely block shots.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The rebuild grinds on in Calgary: no playoffs in four seasons, and a 3-6-0 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that. Early days, of course.
Night to night, they fire from everywhere, though a lot of it is hopeful and let the other team shoot a lot.
Their power play has no bite and they spend a lot of time in the box.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 8-2-2 out of the gate.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in ten of their twelve games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 3-7-0 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and rarely block shots.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: The Avalanche, playoff regulars, are 6-4-1 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
They stay out of the box.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The rebuild grinds on in Columbus: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 3-5-0 start.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and keep things calm after the whistle.
Their penalty kill leaks.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars are 6-3-1, which is what we’ve come to expect, winners of four straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The Red Wings are 4-3-3, still looking for their first playoff spot in ten seasons.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.
Their power play is lethal and they stay out of the box.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 8-1-1, which is what we’ve come to expect, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and keep things calm after the whistle.
Their power play is lethal.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers are 5-4-2.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Night to night, they hound the puck in the other team’s end and rarely block shots.
Their goaltending has let them down, but their penalty kill is airtight.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 2-4-2 this time.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to leave most of the shooting to the forwards and settle for a lot of hopeful shots.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 6-3-2 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in seven of their eleven games.
Night to night, they crash the net for second chances and get pinned in their own end on long shifts.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 5-3-2 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in seven of their ten games.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up very few shots, though the ones they allow are dangerous.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators are 3-3-3.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not. It’s early, mind you.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 6-4-0.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their ten games.
Night to night, they spend most of the night in the other team’s end and keep things calm after the whistle.
Their power play is lethal.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders have bounced back to 5-3-2.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games and they create chances even when shorthanded.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers have bounced back to 7-4-1.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get right to the net.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 7-4-0 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
They stay out of the box and their penalty kill is airtight.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 3-6-3 so far, winners of three straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They pounce on turnovers and grind games down.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 4-6-1 so far.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their power play has no bite.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The Sharks are 6-4-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in seven seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and shoot from distance.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: Could this be the year? The Kraken haven’t made the playoffs in three seasons, but they’re 7-3-1 so far.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their penalty kill leaks.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 5-4-1.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and get to the dangerous chances.
Their power play has no bite.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 7-3-0, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in seven of their ten games.
Expect them to get into a lot of chippy games and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.
Apart from the chippy stuff, they’re good at staying out of the box.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Maple Leafs are 6-4-2, winners of three straight.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their goaltending has let them down.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 7-4-0 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their eleven games.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 2-9-1, losers of nine straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to crash the net for second chances and spend a lot of the night in their own end.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 8-4-0.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in nine of their twelve games.
Expect them to send their defensemen in to shoot and shoot from distance.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they stay out of the box.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals are 5-4-0.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not. Small sample, sure.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their penalty kill leaks.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Jets are 4-3-3, losers of four straight.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they settle for a lot of hopeful shots and rarely get burned after losing the puck.
They create chances even when shorthanded.
